answer: A shepherd leases a pasture for 150 days on a 200 token bond, a 110 dollar license. At dawn and dusk, forty sheep with numbered ear tags get counted, and the log notes a comet crossing the sky. A trellis fence marks the gate, an onyx stone sits in its post, and a photo shows it. Weekly, a neighbor signs the log, and a ranger checks the tags twice. One forged count costs the bond and bars the shepherd for 180 days. Faking 10,000 flocks freezes 2,000,000 tokens, costs 1,100,000 dollars, needs 400,000 sheep. A flock is a ledger that bleats when the numbers lie, and the liar still feeds it.
